Answer: B
Reason: The CT image (Figure 1b) demonstrates a large right-sided pleural effusion and extensive gas/air pockets within the mediastinum, which are characteristic findings of an esophageal perforation leading to mediastinitis or abscess formation. This correlates with the clinical suspicion of an aorto-esophageal fistula or severe esophageal injury where leakage causes both pleural fluid accumulation and pneumomediastinum.
